title: Working with DbContext in EF Core
description: Learn to create databases, save data, and retrieve data using EF Core DbContext.

data.text: Now that we have our entities and DbContext class, let's learn how to interact with the database using EF Core.

data.title: SchoolDbContext
data.content: The DbContext class with DbSet properties and connection configuration

data.text: The context class includes `DbSet<TEntity>` properties for `Student` and `Grade` types, which will be mapped to the `Students` and `Grades` tables in the database.
There are two ways to create a database and schema in EF Core:

items: **EnsureCreated()** - Simple method for testing/prototyping (no schema updates)
**Migration API** - For development with schema evolution

data.title: Complete CRUD Workflow
data.content: Creating database, saving data, and retrieving data

data.caption: EF Core CRUD workflow
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[Create DbContext] --> B[EnsureCreated]
    B --> C[Create Entities]
    C --> D[Add to Context]
    D --> E[SaveChanges]
    E --> F[Query Data]

data.title: EnsureCreated vs Migrations
data.text: EnsureCreated() does not modify the schema if the database exists. Use Migration API for development to sync schema changes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DbContext manages database connections and operations
SaveChanges() persists changes to the database
data.takeaway: Continue to the next module to learn about DbContext configuration and Fluent API.
